title: Quarterly Runboard: scenario-driven commitments & cross-team tradeoff matrix for Hosted API + Model Catalog
creator: Aisha Romero
description:
Purpose: Create a runnable quarterly ‘runboard’ that translates executive OKR targets into discrete, prioritized commitments for the Hosted API and Model Catalog teams. This ticket synthesizes scenario-driven lanes (Base/Surge/Constrained), a cross-team tradeoff matrix (latency vs cost vs availability), and a gated rollout plan that ties canary thresholds to evaluation signals and capacity hedges.

Scope: - Define 3 commitment lanes for Q2 (Base growth, Holiday-surge prep, Constrained capacity fallback). - Map each lane to specific model lineup decisions (retain/rotate/quantize) and infra knobs (batching, prefix cache, autoscale policies). - Produce a decision matrix for tradeoffs with concrete thresholds (latency p95, cost per 1k tokens, SLA availability). - Align PM, Eng, Design owners; produce handoff artifacts for Solutions & CS.

Out-of-scope: Detailed kernel-level runtime changes (ENG will own PRs), deep security design for on-prem (tracked separately in PM-77233).
acceptance_criteria: Runboard document with lane definitions and numeric thresholds published to Confluence
Canary gating plan with automated alerts wired to Console dashboards
Backstop contingency actions (model downgrade, region shift, capacity-burst) enumerated and assigned
milestones: 2026-03-19: Draft runboard + tradeoff matrix for review
2026-04-02: Canary thresholds finalized and automated alerting configured
2026-04-30: Publish runbook and handoff to Ops
okr_mapping: OKR-API-01: Reduce p95 latency on hosted endpoints by 15% (Runboard lanes define acceptable variance)
OKR-COST-02: Lower average per-token serving cost across mission workloads by 12% (includes suggested quantization and batching knobs)
OKR-RELIABILITY-03: Maintain 99.95% SLA for Dedicated customers during base lane; define fallbacks for constrained lane
risks: Model-quality regressions from aggressive quantization — mitigated with eval guardrail and rollback window
Autoscale misconfiguration could introduce flapping under surge lane — require load-test validation and longer stabilization window
Dependence on ENG-19382 (KV cache opt) for promised latency gains — track closely and create contingency path
notes: Tradeoff matrix will enumerate breakpoints (e.g., cost per 1k tokens at 10k qps) and recommend primary/secondary actions for each cell
We will surface runboard status in Console > Runbook tab with three live signals: lane (Base/Surge/Constrained), current lane metrics, and active mitigations
Design will provide a compact UI pattern for runbook visibility and for two-click operator actions (failover to alternate model variant)
Budget holder sign-off required for capacity-burst option in Surge lane
